findings.finding: The original positive consent test claimed signs once but checked challenge/approval counts and signature shape, not actual provider invocation counts. Status-only also lacked zero-provider-invocation evidence. Callback navigation resets window-only counters.
findings.impact: A duplicate-signing or unnecessary status-only provider call regression could pass the browser fixture suite. This is coverage hardening, not evidence of a product defect.
findings.resolution: Added an allowlisted persistent Node recorder via page.exposeFunction; provider stubs record connect/sign call kinds only. Assert exact [connect, sign] for trading and [] for status-only after callback navigation.

Reviewed injected provider return shapes, synthetic 64-byte signature serialization, DOM readiness contracts, response consumption records, and exposeFunction call contract. Exact [connect, sign] and [] assertions now survive callback navigation.

Every one of 14 groups emits a distinct PASS line after meaningful assertions. Page errors and null/undefined provider rejection failures are checked. Recorded call kinds contain no signed bytes, message payload, signature, or key material.

One server and one browser/page are reused; each scenario resets only fixture state and navigates. No expensive repeated external calls or unbounded hot-path computation occurs in intended fixture use.

Reviewed closure capture of active fixture, gate completion ordering, double requestAnimationFrame checkpoints, response.finished plus JSON-read waits, and exposed recorder await sequencing. The exact persistent call assertions and all held-gate groups passed without timing sleeps.
